patients.summary: Healthy high school science teacher who joined in 2021. New hypertension in December 2024 led to a renal CTA showing multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia with renal artery stenosis and renovascular hypertension; the right ICA is also involved. documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT - PREVENTIVE

30 y/o woman establishing care. Teaches chemistry and earth science at a public high school. Feels well. Here mainly to have a doctor of record and get the usual screening done.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FHx: Mom has high blood pressure, diagnosed young (around 32). Dad had an ischemic stroke at 48, recovered. A paternal uncle has narrowing of a kidney artery - she does not know details.
SHx: Never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs. Runs or bikes most days. Lives on her own. Seat belt always.
Gyn: regular cycles. Last Pap 2019 at prior office, normal per pt; records requested.
Vaccines: Tdap 2017; Pfizer x2 this spring through the school district clinic.

ROS: negative in full - no headaches, no chest pain, no palpitations, no GI or GU complaints, mood good.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP normal. Well appearing. HEENT clear, TM normal, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses, no bruit. Skin without notable lesions. Extremities warm, pulses full. Neuro grossly normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment/Plan:
Healthy adult, preventive care.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screens discussed and drawn.
- Pap due next year (3 yr from 2019); will do co-testing at next physical.
- Flu shot and COVID booster this fall when available.
- Annual visits. Message anytime.

documents.title: Office Visit - Headaches, High Blood Pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: headaches and tiredness for several weeks.

HPI: 33 y/o teacher, healthy, last seen 8/2023 with normal BP. Over the past several weeks she has had near-daily dull headaches and is unusually tired. MA found her pressure high on rooming, and I rechecked both arms after she'd sat 5 min: 168/100 right and left. She has had no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no palpitations. No vision change, no focal weakness. No meds, no OTC decongestants or NSAIDs, no supplements, no energy drinks. Not on hormonal contraception.

FHx: mother hypertensive from about age 32; father ischemic stroke at 48; paternal uncle with renal artery stenosis.
SHx: never smoker, no alcohol, active, exercises most days.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 168/100 both arms. BMI 23. Comfortable. Fundi: sharp discs, normal vessels, no hemorrhages or exudates. Neck: supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen: soft, nontender, there is a bruit on the right near the umbilicus. No palpable masses. Ext: radial and femoral pulses equal, no delay, no edema. Neuro nonfocal.
ECG in office: normal.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Hypertension, new, stage 2 range. Young, lean, active, no meds - and an abdominal bruit plus that family history (uncle with renal artery stenosis). A renovascular cause such as fibromuscular dysplasia has to be excluded first.
 - BMP, UA, TSH, lipids today.
 - CT angiogram of the renal arteries ordered; will need prior auth.
 - Start home BP monitoring, twice daily for a week, bring the log. Lower sodium, keep exercising.
 - Holding off on medication until imaging is back; she prefers to start with lifestyle and I think that's reasonable for a couple of weeks.
2. Headaches - likely pressure-related. Return precautions reviewed (thunderclap headache, neuro symptoms, chest pain - go to ED).
Physical exam overdue; will fold preventive items in at a later visit.

documents.title: Monday's results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Angela - your kidney function, electrolytes, thyroid, cholesterol and urine test are all normal. That's reassuring, but it doesn't rule out a problem with the arteries to the kidneys, so the CT angiogram is still the important next step. We're working on the insurance approval and will call you to schedule. Keep the BP log going.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
EXAM: CT angiography of the abdomen and pelvis, renal artery protocol, with IV contrast. Arterial-phase thin sections with multiplanar and 3D reconstructions.
INDICATION: 33-year-old woman with new hypertension and abdominal bruit.
FINDINGS: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber with no aneurysm or dissection. Single renal artery on each side. Both main renal arteries show a beaded contour in their mid and distal segments, with alternating short segments of narrowing and dilation. No renal artery aneurysm. No dissection flap. The celiac axis, superior and inferior mesenteric arteries and iliac arteries are normal. Kidneys are normal in size and enhance symmetrically, with no infarct, scarring or hydronephrosis. Adrenal glands normal. Liver, spleen, pancreas and bowel unremarkable. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Beaded appearance of both main renal arteries, consistent with multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia. Normal kidneys. No aneurysm or dissection.

conditions.label: Fibromuscular dysplasia
conditions.note: multifocal, both renal arteries on CTA

orders.reason: fibromuscular dysplasia of renal arteries with hypertension; vascular evaluation

documents.title: Result call - CTA
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt on her lunch break with the CTA result. Both renal arteries have the beaded look of multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia. Kidneys themselves look normal, no aneurysm.

Explained what FMD is (a non-atherosclerotic condition of the artery wall, much more common in women, can affect other arteries too), and that it fits the high pressures. Given her uncle, she is not completely surprised.

Plan: referral to cardiology (vascular medicine) for FMD evaluation, including whether other arteries are involved. Keep the home log, low sodium. She will send her BP log through the portal.
Referral placed, records to go with it.

documents.author: front desk

events.reason: CT angiogram head and neck, ordered by cardiology

reports.text:
EXAM: CT angiography of the head and neck with IV contrast, with multiplanar and 3D reconstructions.
INDICATION: Fibromuscular dysplasia of the renal arteries; screening of cervical and intracranial vessels.
FINDINGS: Aortic arch normal with conventional branching. Right internal carotid artery: in its mid to distal cervical segment there are alternating areas of narrowing and dilation. No dissection or pseudoaneurysm. Left internal carotid artery, both common carotid arteries and both vertebral arteries are normal. Intracranial: the circle of Willis is intact with no aneurysm, no stenosis and no vascular malformation. The brain parenchyma on source images is unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Alternating narrowing and dilation of the right internal carotid artery, consistent with fibromuscular dysplasia. No intracranial aneurysm. No dissection.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation - Vascular Medicine
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - VASCULAR MEDICINE CLINIC
Date of service: 03/24/2025
Re: Angela Duffy, DOB 05/06/1991
Referred by: primary care, for fibromuscular dysplasia of the renal arteries

Thank you for sending Ms. Duffy, a 33-year-old science teacher you saw in December for new hypertension, at which time an abdominal bruit led to a renal CTA showing beading of both main renal arteries.

Since then the headaches have persisted. For about the past month she has also noticed a pulsing, whooshing noise in the right ear, in time with her heartbeat. She has had some neck stiffness off and on. A pharmacy machine read high when she checked it in February. No visual loss, no transient weakness or numbness, no speech trouble. No flank pain.
Review of systems: no asthma, sinus problems, blood in the urine, or skin changes; no fevers, rashes, numbness or tingling in the extremities, or coughing up blood.

Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with hypertension from age 32; father with ischemic stroke at 48; paternal uncle with renal artery stenosis.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Teaches high school science.

Exam: BP 160/100 mmHg in each arm. Well appearing. There is a bruit over the right carotid. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Peripheral pulses symmetric. Neurologic examination normal - cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation normal, gait normal.

Data:
- Renal CTA 01/08/2025 (reviewed): beaded mid-distal main renal arteries on both sides, typical of multifocal FMD; kidneys normal.
- CTA head and neck 03/10/2025: alternating narrowing and dilation of the right internal carotid artery; no intracranial aneurysm; no dissection.
- Labs 03/10/2025: plasma renin activity 8.6 ng/mL/h (high); aldosterone 26 ng/dL (high). Hepatitis B surface antigen negative, hepatitis C antibody nonreactive, ANA negative. ANCA reported as indeterminate; with imaging this typical of FMD I would not pursue it further.

Impression:
1. Multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia involving both renal arteries and the right internal carotid artery.
2. Renal artery stenosis from FMD, with secondary (renovascular) hypertension - high renin and aldosterone support this.

Recommendations:
- Low-sodium diet, continue regular exercise, home BP log twice daily.
- Blood pressure management to continue through primary care.
- Return to vascular clinic for follow-up; we will review her pressures and the renal arteries then.

Thank you for the referral.
Cardiology / Vascular Medicine
Allergies: NKDA

PREVENTIVE VISIT + PROBLEM VISIT

34 y/o, on February/March break. Problems: multifocal FMD (both renal arteries, right ICA), renal artery stenosis with renovascular hypertension. Meds: amlodipine 10 mg daily - takes it every morning, no side effects. NKDA.

Interval: still some headaches. Home readings run about where ours do despite the higher dose. Never got the vascular follow-up booked - their office lost the referral request, she says.
Health maintenance: Pap/HPV 2022 normal, next 2027. HIV/HCV screened 2021. Vaccines current for the season.
SHx: never smoker, no alcohol, running less this winter.

Exam: BP 162/98 (rechecked, similar). Weight stable, BMI ~23. Well. Fundi normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Neuro nonfocal. Skin normal.
PHQ-9: 2.

1. Renovascular HTN / renal artery stenosis from FMD - uncontrolled on full-dose amlodipine. She needs vascular cardiology back in the loop now; new referral sent today and I asked our referral coordinator to confirm the appointment. Continue amlodipine 10 mg. Home log.
2. FMD with carotid involvement - no new neuro symptoms. Reviewed stroke warning signs.
3. Preventive - CBC, CMP, lipids today. Pap not due. Flu/COVID in the fall.
Return once cardiology has seen her.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up - Vascular Medicine
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - VASCULAR MEDICINE CLINIC
Date of service: 06/10/2026
Re: Angela Duffy, DOB 05/06/1991

Ms. Duffy returns, now 35, for multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia (both renal arteries, right internal carotid) with renal artery stenosis and renovascular hypertension, hypertensive since late 2024. Since we saw her in March 2025 her PCP started amlodipine, now 10 mg daily, which she takes faithfully. Even so her home systolic readings sit between 160 and 170 and the headaches continue. She is occasionally lightheaded. Otherwise her review of systems is unremarkable.

She has no personal history of heart disease, diabetes or high cholesterol. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Medications: amlodipine 10 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 164/98. No focal neurologic deficits. Bruits are heard over both flanks. Heart regular. Lungs clear.

Labs today: creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. Plasma renin activity 9.1 ng/mL/h, elevated.

Assessment: renovascular hypertension from FMD-related renal artery stenosis, worsening despite adherence to amlodipine 10 mg, with persistently high renin.

Plan:
- Renal angiography with balloon angioplasty, which is the treatment of choice for renal FMD when pressure stays uncontrolled. Risks, benefits and alternatives discussed; she would like to proceed. Being scheduled at the regional hospital catheterization lab.
- Continue amlodipine 10 mg until then.
- We will send the procedure report.

Cardiology / Vascular Medicine

documents.title: Renal Angiography and Right Renal Artery Angioplasty
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - CARDIAC CATHETERIZATION LABORATORY
Procedure date: 07/28/2026
Patient: Angela Duffy, DOB 05/06/1991
Indication: renovascular hypertension from multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia, uncontrolled on amlodipine 10 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.

Procedures: selective bilateral renal angiography; translesional pressure measurement; balloon angioplasty of the right renal artery.
Access: right common femoral artery, ultrasound-guided, 6 French sheath. Moderate sedation.

Findings:
- Right renal artery: beaded mid and distal main renal artery typical of multifocal FMD, with a significant translesional pressure gradient.
- Left renal artery: beaded mid segment without a significant gradient.
- No aneurysm or dissection.

Intervention: right renal artery balloon angioplasty without stent. After angioplasty the beading was smoothed and the gradient resolved. No dissection on final images.
Closure: closure device to the femoral site, hemostasis achieved.
Complications: none. Estimated blood loss minimal.

Disposition: observed in recovery, femoral site clean, ambulating; discharged home the same afternoon.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily (new); continue amlodipine 10 mg daily.
Follow-up: renal artery duplex ultrasound in about one month at the vascular clinic, then clinic visit to decide on medication adjustment. Home BP log.
Copy to primary care.

documents.body: Great to hear, Angela. We received the procedure report. Keep taking your medicines the way cardiology listed and keep your home log. They'll decide on any changes after the ultrasound - please let us know what they say, and message us if you get dizzy or your readings drop low.
